ei.title: Getbol: A Treasure House with Great Potential
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Getbol, a Symbol of Biodiversity Have you ever visited the Korean tidal flats known as getbol? Getbol is a muddy and flat environment that is exposed at low tide and is covered by water at high tide. Soil on land has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years, creating one of the thickest tidal layers in the world. Since the soil includes organic matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in nutrients and provides habitats for thousands of species. In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 globally threatened or near-threatened species. Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year. For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location. Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would become extinct. Since getbol is not only a unique ecosystem crowded with diverse species but also a resting place for endangered birds, it was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021. The list includes the four tidal flats on the western and southern coasts of Korea: Seocheon Getbol, Gochang Getbol, Shinan Getbol, and Boseong-Suncheon Getbol. Climate Change and Carbon When people think of a changing climate, images of melting glaciers and polar bears losing their habitat often come to mind. But this is only one aspect of the problem. Climate change is causing extreme weather conditions, which have become more frequent and intense worldwide. Heatwaves, droughts, floods, and wildfires are affecting countries around the world. In the autumn of 2019, for example, Australia was hit by one of the worst wildfires on record. Over six months, the wildfires burned about 10 million hectares of land, and killed hundreds of millions of animals. Approximately 30 percent of the koalas in the region are said to have been killed due to the fires. This is why the international community has been seeking solutions to the climate crisis. In 2015, 195 countries signed the Paris Agreement to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. The countries agreed upon the fact that the increase in atmospheric carbon is a major reason for climate change. One key strategy to combat it is to achieve “carbon neutrality,” which involves maintaining a balance between the amount of carbon emitted and carbon absorbed. The Earth’s Atmosphere Is Like a Bathtub Let’s imagine that the Earth’s atmosphere is a large bathtub, and the greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere are like water flowing from a tap into the bathtub. At the bottom of the bathtub, there’s a drain that lets the water out. If we keep the tap running, the water level in the bathtub will rise, just as greenhouse gas emissions have led to an increase in atmospheric carbon. This rise in carbon levels has already resulted in negative environmental consequences, such as climate change. To make matters worse, if the water is not effectively drained, the bathtub will overflow. In other words, if we don't reduce carbon emissions sufficiently, atmospheric carbon will continue to accumulate. Blue Carbon and Getbol One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon in the atmosphere is to use the “good” carbon on Earth. The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon. Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas. It causes the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming and climate change. Green carbon, on the other hand, is carbon absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as rainforests like the Amazon in South America. It plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem because it absorbs carbon dioxide through photosynthesis. Finally, blue carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. The carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is about 50 times faster than that of land ecosystems. Blue carbon can store up to 10 times more carbon per unit area than forests on land, making it highly cost-effective. A notable example of blue carbon can be found in tidal flats located around the ocean. Research conducted in 2021 has revealed that getbol in Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year. This means that getbol alone can offset the carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars in a year. Considering that getbol contains numerous organisms and marine animals that store carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has become a promising and sustainable solution to the current environmental problem. Scientists worldwide are continuing to explore the capabilities of tidal flats with the goal of having them officially recognized as blue carbon. Efforts to Protect Getbol Getbol in Korea was once considered useless muddy land, so much of it has been reclaimed for farming and urbanization. This has led to a decline in the area of tidal flats, causing a loss of biodiversity. To prevent further damage to the marine ecosystem, both the government and environmental organizations have been making efforts to protect the tidal flats by regulating unnecessary development. Without further efforts to restore getbol, we would fail to preserve this valuable ecosystem for future generations. Read More Green Your Inbox Email is one of the most widely used forms of communication today. Did you know that the seemingly innocent act of looking through emails or checking your inbox has an environmental impact? In reality, email travels through an energy-consuming network, contributing to climate change on our planet. Storing countless email messages in data centers creates carbon emissions. These data centers rely on huge servers to store and access data at all times. Because the centers use electricity to run the servers and to cool down the large amounts of heat that they generate, they consume a significant amount of fossil fuels. Mike Berners-Lee, the British researcher and author of How Bad Are Bananas?: The Carbon Footprint of Everything, looked at our average email traffic. For example, a short phone-to-phone email has a carbon footprint of 0.2g of CO₂ emissions. But, a long email, which takes about ten minutes to write and three minutes to read on a computer, has a footprint of 17g of CO₂ emissions. So, something as simple as deleting unnecessary email messages can help to save the Earth.

questions.passage: Soil on land has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years, creating one of the (A)[thickest / thinnest] tidal layers in the world. Since the soil includes organic matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in nutrients and (B)[provides / lacks] habitats for thousands of species. In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 globally threatened or near-threatened species. Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year. For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location. Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would become extinct. Since getbol is not only a unique ecosystem (C)[crowded / empty] with diverse species but also a resting place for endangered birds, it was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① thickest(가장 두꺼운)+provides(제공하다)+crowded(붐비는): 8,500년간 흙이 쌓여 세계에서 '가장 두꺼운' 갯벌층을 이루고, 수천 종에게 서식지를 '제공하며', 다양한 종으로 '붐비는' 생태계라는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답

❌ ② thinnest(가장 얇은)는 오랜 세월 쌓여 '가장 두꺼운' 층을 이룬다는 문맥과 반대

❌ ③ lacks(부족하다)는 서식지를 '제공한다'는 문맥과 반대

❌ ④ empty(텅 빈)는 다양한 종으로 '붐비는' 생태계 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: Climate change is causing (A)[extreme / mild] weather conditions, which have become more frequent and intense worldwide. Heatwaves, droughts, floods, and wildfires are affecting countries around the world. In the autumn of 2019, for example, Australia was hit by one of the (B)[worst / best] wildfires on record. Over six months, the wildfires (C)[burned / saved] about 10 million hectares of land, and killed hundreds of millions of animals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① mild(온화한)는 더 잦고 강해진 '극심한' 기상 문맥과 반대

❌ ② best(최고의)는 기록상 '최악의' 산불 문맥과 반대

❌ ③ saved(구한)는 1천만 헥타르를 '태운' 산불 문맥과 반대

✅ ④ extreme(극심한)+worst(최악의)+burned(태웠다): 극심한 기상, 최악의 산불, 그 산불이 땅을 '태웠다'는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답

questions.passage: Green carbon, on the other hand, is carbon absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as rainforests like the Amazon in South America. It plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem because it (A)[absorbs / releases] carbon dioxide through photosynthesis. Finally, blue carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① slower(더 느린)는 육상보다 50배 '더 빠른' 흡수율 문맥과 반대

✅ ② absorbs(흡수하다)+faster(더 빠른)+cost-effective(비용 효율적인): 그린 카본이 광합성으로 이산화탄소를 '흡수하고', 해양 생태계 흡수율이 육상보다 50배 '더 빠르며', 단위 면적당 10배 저장해 '비용 효율적'이라는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답

❌ ③ releases(방출하다)는 이산화탄소를 '흡수한다'는 문맥과 반대

❌ ④ wasteful(낭비적인)은 육상보다 훨씬 효율적이라는 '비용 효율적' 문맥과 반대

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ common → unique: 갯벌은 다양한 종으로 붐비는 '독특한' 생태계다
det.analysis:
✅ ① biodiversity: 풍부한 '생물 다양성' 덕분에 철새가 찾아온다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ② extinct: 갯벌이 없으면 쉴 곳이 없어 '멸종할' 것이라는 문맥에 적절

❌ ③ common(흔한) → unique(독특한): 갯벌은 다양한 종으로 붐비는 '독특한' 생태계이므로 unique가 맞다. common은 UNESCO 세계자연유산에 등재된 갯벌의 특별함과 반대 ← 정답

✅ ④ endangered: 멸종 위기에 처한 '위기의' 새들의 쉼터라는 문맥에 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② better → worse: 상황을 '악화시키는' 것은 물이 배출되지 않아 욕조가 넘치는 것이다
det.analysis:
✅ ① drain: 욕조 바닥에 물을 내보내는 '배수구'가 있다는 문맥에 적절

❌ ② better(더 좋게) → worse(더 나쁘게): 물이 효과적으로 빠지지 않으면 욕조가 넘친다는 것은 상황을 '악화'시키는 것이므로 worse가 맞다. better는 정반대 ← 정답

✅ ③ reduce: 탄소 배출을 충분히 '줄이지' 않으면 대기 탄소가 계속 쌓인다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ④ accumulate: 대기 중 탄소가 계속 '축적된다'는 문맥에 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ destroy → preserve: 미래 세대를 위해 이 소중한 생태계를 '보존하다'
det.analysis:
✅ ① reclaimed: 갯벌이 농사와 도시화를 위해 '개간되었다'는 문맥에 적절

✅ ② decline: 갯벌 면적의 '감소'로 생물 다양성이 줄었다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ③ prevent: 해양 생태계에 대한 추가 피해를 '막기' 위해 노력한다는 문맥에 적절

❌ ④ destroy(파괴하다) → preserve(보존하다): 복원 노력이 없으면 이 소중한 생태계를 '보존하지' 못한다는 문맥이므로 preserve가 맞다. destroy는 정반대 ← 정답

questions.passage: Soil on land has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years, creating one of the thickest tidal layers in the world.  Since the soil includes organic matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in __________ and provides habitats for thousands of species.  In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 globally threatened or near-threatened species.  Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① nutrients(영양분): 흙에 육지 동식물의 유기물이 포함되어 있어 갯벌이 '영양분'이 풍부하고 수천 종에게 서식지를 제공한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답

❌ ② pollution(오염): 서식지를 제공하는 풍부함과 반대되는 부정적 개념

❌ ③ danger(위험): 유기물이 풍부한 흙이 주는 것은 위험이 아님

❌ ④ noise(소음): 영양·서식지 문맥과 전혀 무관
det.tip: organic matter(유기물)가 풍부한 흙 → nutrients(영양분)가 풍부

det.analysis:
❌ ① conflict(갈등): 배출량과 흡수량의 균형을 맞춘다는 문맥과 무관

❌ ② increase(증가): 탄소 중립은 늘리는 것이 아니라 맞추는 것이므로 반대

✅ ③ balance(균형): '탄소 중립'은 배출되는 탄소량과 흡수되는 탄소량 사이의 '균형'을 유지하는 것이라는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답

❌ ④ gap(격차): 균형을 유지한다는 문맥과 반대되는 벌어짐의 개념

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① combustion(연소): 이산화탄소를 흡수하는 과정이 아니라 태워 배출하는 과정

✅ ② photosynthesis(광합성): 그린 카본은 식물이 흡수·저장하며, 이산화탄소를 '광합성'을 통해 흡수한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답

❌ ③ evaporation(증발): 물이 기체로 변하는 현상으로 탄소 흡수와 무관

❌ ④ radiation(복사): 열·에너지 방출로 이산화탄소 흡수 과정과 무관

❌ ② honest: 정직한 (innocent의 '순진한' 뜻과 비슷해 반대가 아님)

❌ ③ quiet: 조용한 (무해함과 무관한 개념)

❌ ④ gentle: 온화한 (해로움의 반대가 아니라 순한 성질)

questions.passage:
(A) The ocean can <u>store</u> a large amount of carbon, keeping it safely away from the atmosphere for hundreds of years. Marine plants and mud hold it deep below the surface.
(B) On my way home, I stopped by a small <u>store</u> near the bus stop to buy some milk and fresh bread for dinner.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 store의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) can store a large amount of carbon는 바다가 탄소를 대기에서 격리해 '저장한다'는 동사이고, (B) a small store near the bus stop은 우유와 빵을 사러 들른 '가게'라는 명사 ← 정답

❌ ① (A)는 '가게'가 아니라 탄소를 '저장하다'

❌ ③ (A)의 store는 '창고'라는 명사가 아니라 '저장하다'라는 동사

❌ ④ (B)의 store는 '상점'으로 맞지만 (A)는 '쌓다'가 아니라 '저장하다'

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the natural home or environment where an animal or plant normally lives"

det.analysis:
❌ ① glacier: 빙하 (얼음이 오랜 세월 쌓여 형성된 거대한 얼음덩이)

❌ ② emission: 배출(물) (기체나 물질이 대기로 뿜어져 나오는 것)

❌ ③ nutrient: 영양분 (생물이 자라는 데 필요한 양분)

✅ ④ habitat: 서식지 (동식물이 자연적으로 살아가는 보금자리·환경) ← 정답

questions.passage: One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon in the atmosphere is to use the "good" carbon on Earth. The Earth's carbon can be __________ (divide) into three types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: divide(동사, 나누다) → divided(과거분사): 빈칸은 조동사 can 뒤 be동사와 함께 쓰이는 자리이므로 'can be + 과거분사'의 수동태가 되어야 한다. '지구의 탄소는 세 종류로 나뉠 수 있다'는 뜻이 되도록 동사원형 divide를 과거분사 divided로 바꾼다.

questions.passage: __________ (consider) that getbol contains numerous organisms and marine animals that store carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has become a promising and sustainable solution to the current environmental problem. Scientists worldwide are continuing to explore the capabilities of tidal flats with the goal of having them officially recognized as blue carbon.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: consider(동사, 고려하다) → considering(현재분사): 빈칸은 주절 앞에서 이유·전제를 나타내는 분사구문의 자리이므로 현재분사가 와야 한다. 'Considering that ~'은 '~을 고려하면'이라는 뜻의 관용적 분사구문으로, 동사원형 consider를 현재분사 considering으로 바꾼다.

questions.passage: Did you know that the seemingly innocent act of looking through emails or checking your inbox has an environmental impact?  In reality, email travels through an energy-consuming network, __________ on our planet.  Storing countless email messages in data centers creates carbon emissions.  These data centers rely on huge servers to store and access data at all times.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 contributing to climate change(기후 변화에 일조하다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① saving our planet(지구를 구하다): 이메일이 에너지를 소비해 탄소를 배출한다는 흐름과 반대

❌ ② reducing carbon emissions(탄소 배출을 줄이다): 오히려 배출을 늘린다는 문맥과 반대

✅ ③ contributing to climate change(기후 변화에 일조하다): 이메일이 에너지 소모 네트워크를 거치고 데이터 센터가 탄소를 배출한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답

❌ ④ protecting the environment(환경을 보호하다): 환경에 악영향을 준다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: energy-consuming network + carbon emissions → contributing to climate change(기후 변화에 일조)

questions.passage: It plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem because it absorbs carbon dioxide through photosynthesis.  Finally, blue carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes.  The carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is about 50 times faster than that of land ecosystems.  Blue carbon can store up to 10 times more carbon per unit area than forests on land, making it __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① highly cost-effective(매우 비용 효율적인): 블루 카본이 단위 면적당 육지 숲보다 10배 많은 탄소를 저장할 수 있다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답

❌ ② totally useless(완전히 쓸모없는): 10배 저장 효율이라는 긍정적 문맥과 반대

❌ ③ very dangerous(매우 위험한): 탄소 저장의 이점을 설명하는 문맥과 무관

❌ ④ quite ordinary(꽤 평범한): 뛰어난 저장 효율을 강조하는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 단위 면적당 10배 저장 → highly cost-effective(매우 비용 효율적)
